candidate.title: Nextera Rapid Capture
candidate.scope: The single Nextera Rapid Capture target-enrichment route depicted in the assigned Illumina schematic. It starts with already denatured and pooled Nextera library fragments, adds a biotinylated target probe, hybridizes, captures on magnetic beads, and elutes a target-containing library product ready for cluster generation. There are no depicted alternatives or independent branches. Upstream specimen identity, biological origin of the target, and construction of the Nextera input library are outside this depiction; the surrounding RNA-poster context does not establish an RNA-to-cDNA operation here. The retained library fragment represents a selected target sequence, rather than a newly synthesized probe-derived readout. Enrichment and downstream readout interpretation are schematic deductions, not measurements of specificity or abundance.

features: Denaturation and pooling are stated preparation history of the input, not separately drawn transformations.
Several offset linear fragments form the pool; one is highlighted with a dark blue region labeled Target. The faint fragments have no separate outgoing route.
Colored terminal regions correspond to the adapter/index arrangement labeled on the final product.

states.label: Biotinylated target probe

states.label: Target-containing library fragment hybridized to biotinylated probe

Thus the target-bearing library fragment is the depicted readout carrier; the probe provides selection. Enrichment is qualitative and does not establish perfect specificity or quantitative recovery.

states.label: Eluted target-containing library product ready for cluster generation

The target sequence is carried within the retained library fragment. The drawing labels two index regions but does not give index sequences or sample assignments.
This is a material endpoint for cluster generation; no sequence-data output or quantitative readout is drawn.

operations.label: Hybridize probes to targets
operations.description: Add the biotinylated target probe to the already denatured and pooled Nextera fragments. The depicted target-containing library fragment changes from a free strand to a probe-library hybrid with the short probe paired at its target region.
operations.mechanism: Target-probe hybridization, as explicitly labeled and drawn. The probe remains biotinylated in the hybrid.
operations.information_effect: Associates a selectable probe with the target region of a pre-existing library fragment. The retained library molecule, including its flanking regions, carries the target sequence.

method_scopes.rationale: The card and figure title identify a single target method, Nextera Rapid Capture. All three depicted transformation instances belong to its capture component at the declared schematic scope. Nextera library describes the prepared input, not an additional alternative target workflow. The catalogue description supplies only the method name, and no publications or version-specific implementation claims are supplied.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports the candidate at its declared schematic scope. All three depicted transformations and their material interfaces are represented, with no omitted alternative or retained branch. The same target-bearing library fragment persists through hybridization, bead attachment, and elution; the short biotinylated probe provides selection rather than the final readout carrier. P5, both index labels, Target, and P7 are preserved. The candidate distinguishes depicted content from qualitative enrichment/readout deductions and does not claim perfect specificity, quantitative recovery, a biological specimen, or an unshown conversion. The supplied catalogue has no publications, the card requires no primary-paper match, and the empty paper_matches therefore makes no false verification claim. No consequential source conflict or architecture-changing unknown is apparent.
